differences.what: Wire-count derivation: A gives the neighbour counts z_b=3*C(97,2)=13968 and z_c=C(97,3)+3*97=147731, the ordered-pair count vz of side wires per invocation, and c_b=100, c_c=101 central wires feeding W=2N+I(vz+c); B gives only I=3v^2 and the final W_b, W_c values.

items.note: Both plans carry B1-B4 (A S1.4.2.1-S1.4.2.3, S1.4.3; B S1.3.1.1-S1.3.1.3, S1.3.2) correctly. A adds the neighbour and central-wire counts behind W_b and W_c, a constant-level difference.

Both plans state the frame invariant, why a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and the route operator for every role including auxiliaries (A S1.5.1-S1.5.2, B S1.4.1-S1.4.3).

differences.what: Residual table: B lists each edge's orthogonal residual subspace (B(x)t_X^perp, P(x)t_X^perp, B(x)F, P(x)F, B(x)<t_Y>, ..., (A(x)F)(x)Q^perp) with its dimension; A gives only the dimensions.
Side edge 2->5: B gives the residual P(x)<t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2, made possible by t_X perp t_Y; A gives only the dimension h-2 and the orthogonality, not the complement.
Gate-label table eq:motif-labels for times 0-7, and the central wire's single return from A(x)F to B(x)F losing P(x)F; B never gives the gate labels.

items.note: Under the checklist B carries L1-L5 in full, while A has L1 and L2 only partially (dimensions without the residual subspaces or the complement). A's gate-label table is a real counterweight but is not a checklist sub-step.

differences.what: A states the full matrix assignment (P_U at gates and sinks, -P_{U_a} at X_a, zero at the other sources), that reversing an edge only negates P_V-P_U so decreasing edges keep rank equal to the dimension change, the numeric s_b, and the endpoint case for the other roles (zero source, identity sink). B gives only the projection rank, the 2P_{U_a} exception and I_m.
B defines the shear frame Phi_M as moving (H,D) to (H+MD,D); A uses frames Phi_{M_v} without defining them, though it states the shear in the matrix-shear lemma.

items.note: A covers the proof at lines 1156-1171 more completely: the assignment, the reversed-edge rank and the other-role endpoints. B's explicit Phi_M definition weighs less.

differences.what: Endpoints: A states that the zero label has frame I and the full label C^{(x)m}, that X_a->Y_a carries C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) and C elsewhere, the repair by Z before and i^{27k}Z after via C=iZC^{-1}Z, and the negation of the X outputs. B gives only 'source and sink corrections (C=iZC^{-1}Z on the 27 coordinates)' and 'undoing the signed exchange'.
B states that each basis vector has odd weight, so the phase is i^{eps[v.x]} = (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^{v.x}. A gives the Hadamard step and the kernel but not the odd weight.

items.note: Both plans have P1 and s_c; neither states P3 explicitly. A's full P4 against B's partial P4 outweighs B's fuller P2, where A lacks only the odd-weight remark.

differences.what: The complex deficit eta_c = 73/19906842167500 is stated by B and absent from A.
B derives s_b/W_b < m^tau and s_c/W_c < m^sigma from both deficits exceeding 20*2^{-50} and log m < 20. A derives only the bit case and later just asserts s/W <= m^sigma for the complex recurrence.

items.note: Both plans have R1 and R2. A lacks R3 entirely and the complex half of R4, so the exponent sigma of the butterfly-layer recurrence is never derived in A.

differences.what: B derives the elementary operations (split into q^2 streams; row split r=Wg+w giving W equal-shape streams of volume V/W) and the controlled-shift lemma (offset work absorbed because b^C=O(q^b); multiplication by c coprime to q via c increasing pieces). A states the operations and only the split-at-Q-a method.

items.note: Supporting item. B reconstructs more of the proofs at lines 513-604; A mostly restates the lemmas.

differences.what: Elimination proof: B clears entries to the left of the pivot by right multiplication and entries below it by left multiplication with lower-triangular elementary matrices, deletes the pivot row and column and repeats on the active indices, and takes E_1=L^{-1}, E_2=R^{-1}. A gives only the pivot choice and the conclusion.

items.note: Both plans carry M2-M4 (A S1.7.1.5.2-S1.7.1.5.3; B S1.7.1-S1.7.4). Only B carries M1 in full.

Both plans carry the same steps: the row split into W role streams, Phi_{A_e} per edge by recursive interchanges, the frame identity giving H<-H+D on every row, the three updates, s calls on V/W, the recurrence and its geometric sum, and the depth-first fixed-tape schedule (A S1.7.1.6-S1.7.1.12; B S1.8.1-S1.8.7).

differences.what: B has the high digits interchanged one pair at a time and joined into a row field R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, with rho=ceil(k log W/(2 log q)), and the padded rows scanned away and the joining moves reversed at the end. A says only that the top O(log e) digits are moved into a row field.

items.note: Supporting item. Both plans have the padding, the base-m pieces, the binary padding and the one-bit case. B describes the row-field construction more faithfully.

Both plans give the Gaussian dyadic identities, the conjugation by P_M, one forward child per residual vector via the (C^{-1})^{(x)f} identity, s_c children on f=e/m axes, H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D, and basis changes as row additions (A S1.8.1.4-S1.8.1.6, S1.8.2, S1.8.4; B S2.1.4-S2.1.8, S2.2.10).

differences.what: The packed cyclic shift y <- y +- sum_i 2^{j_i}[x_{j_i}=1][z_{j_i}=b] mod 2^{fK}, a bijection because the offset never depends on its target, which is how one line acts on all segments at once. B has no such formula.
The omitted top selected position j_{f-1}, supplied afterwards by one two-bit XOR in O(V).
The explicit time bound O(V(L^tau+1)+M A^3 + delta_bad M A (R+A)), with its scan and radix-pass terms. A gives the movement cost and says the repair terms are negligible.

items.note: Both plans have the eight operations and their cycles, the guards, the union bound and the T_0 S_0^{-1} repair. A's packing formula and the top-position case are derivation steps; B's explicit cost terms add completeness only.

Both plans give the individual kernels, the node overhead, rows from the first q_0 chunks, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the internal and leaf sums and the base-m pieces giving d^{lambda'} (A S1.8.5-S1.8.10; B S2.3.1-S2.3.8). B lists the lambda conditions abstractly; A uses beta=1/2 and the fixed values. These are equivalent.

differences.what: Guard constants: B defines nu=min{j: m^j>=B}, C_1=max{20,nu+3} and C_0=128mB^2. A uses C_0 without defining it.

items.note: Both plans carry S2-S5 (A S1.8.12-S1.8.14; B S2.4.2-S2.4.7, S2.5). B's S1 is complete while A's lacks C_0.

Both plans give character cancellation by the y^{rj_0}=-1 pairing, decimation in frequency with bit-reversed storage and the reversed procedure, rounds as a parallel butterfly plus a monomial J_E, the layout L (prefix moves, O(p/K) chunk exchanges), the per-round costs and the l*sqrt2*2^{-p} error. Small extras run both ways: A names the moved slots, B gives the formula for E.

Both plans give evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the four products, |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, two's-complement packing, centred extraction, negacyclic reduction and the shift by p+l (A S2.2.1-S2.2.5; B S3.4.1-S3.4.6).
Both plans have the convolution identity with scaling by M, P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), the 3*delta+eta error giving sqrt2*M(3l+1)2^{-p}, and the O(Tp log(rp)) products (A S2.3-S2.5; B S3.5.1-S3.5.6).

differences.what: B defines S'=S/2, J'=N^{-1}/2 and D'=2^{-(2alpha^2-2)}D with ||S'||<3/4, ||J'||<7/8, ||D'||<1, which is why A and B_0 are contractions, and gives the three routines' time bounds. A names A=S/2 and B_0=D'J'C without defining J', D' or bounding them.

items.note: Both plans have the Gaussian identity, the Neumann inversion, the normalisation product 2^{-2alpha^2}, the dropped sorts, the tensoring and the axis exposure. B also justifies the contraction property.

Both plans give the chirp period, the Bluestein coefficient check, F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+ tensoring to RF^+R=F^+, the normalised convolution rule giving (u*v)/S^2, and the conjugation (A S4.1-S4.4; B S4.2.1-S4.2.6).

Both plans give the fixed rationals and their inequalities, the sizes and comparison constants, alpha and gamma, the prime-count bound exceeding d, Bernoulli for T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta>p, and the trial-division setup. Minor extras run both ways: A has the disjoint intervals, B has x>e^{2/eta}.

differences.what: B has the zero padding inserted by one nested lexicographic scan in O(Tp), and the reason for the update order i=d,...,1: the lower-index controls still hold the original digits.

items.note: Supporting item. Both plans have the isomorphism, the triangular formula and the shifts that keep the padding zero. B adds the padding scan and the justification of the update order.

differences.what: B shows Theta well defined because (zeta y)^r=(-1)(-1)=1, and an isomorphism because it is diagonal with nonzero zeta^k. A gives only the wrap identity.

items.note: Supporting item. Both plans have the wrap check, the formula for M_C and the computed twist. B also proves the isomorphism.

Both plans give the source transform and its exact counterpart RF_s, the conjugate procedure, the chirp transform formulas, the six steps and the roles of the two factors S together with 2^{2b+4} (A S6, S6.3-S6.4; B S5.3-S5.8, S5.9.2.1).

Both plans chain E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, (2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L and 448b*2^{-3b/4}<1/2, then round and propagate carries. A itemises the individual error terms; B states the contraction principle as a step. The coverage is equivalent.

differences.what: B justifies table rows 4-7: O(d^2) axis moves each costing O(V(1+l^tau)) plus O(dV) CRT rotations; Gaussian lines summing to O(dTp^{3/2+delta}alpha) with alpha=Theta(p^{1/4+eps/2}); chirps at O(dp^{1+delta}) per entry; packed products at O(Tp log(rp)) without calling the new algorithm. A justifies only rows 1-3 and the setup and exceptional costs.

items.note: Both plans have the table, the margins with min=2^{-181}=2kappa, the o(V) setup and repair costs, and the final bound with the schoolbook cutoff. B derives more of the rows.

differences.what: B's top-level claim states that the bound disproves the n log n conjecture in this model. A never draws this conclusion. Neither plan gives the liminf argument.

items.note: B at least states the item's conclusion; A only lists the conjecture as background.

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route: network, frames, labels, then the two fast procedures, then synthetic transforms, resampling, chirp and the algorithm, then exact recovery and costs. B derives s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m and both exponents tau and sigma from the exact deficits in one step that feeds both recurrences. A derives tau for the bit network but only asserts s/W<=m^sigma for the butterfly-layer recurrence, so the complex branch of the central saving thins in A.

overall.reason: Neither plan has an error. The decisive difference is in the central saving: B derives both exponents from the exact deficits (eta_b, eta_c > 20*2^{-50}, giving s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma), while A omits eta_c and only asserts the complex exponent used by the layer recurrence. Among the other core items the slight differences balance: A has the wire counts, the bit-matrix assignment, the phase endpoints P4 and the packed shift; B has residual table L1-L2, elimination M1, the guard constant C_0 and the cost-row derivations. B adds several slight gains on supporting items.
